note: Adapted from Hill (1927), Memoirs of the National Museum, Melbourne 7, pp. 96-98; the original combination is Mirotermes melvillensis (Hill, 1915). The soldier and worker were described by Hill (1915); only the alate and supplementary soldier measurements are given here. The measurement table is badly damaged in the OCR and is not transcribed.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate with a broad, rounded head, flat on the summit; eyes large, prominent and coarsely faceted; ocelli large, broadly oval and close to the eyes; antennae 14-jointed, the 3rd joint smallest, the 4th and 5th equal; pronotum slightly concave and turned up in front, the anterolateral angles broadly rounded. The soldier and worker were described by Hill (1915); this paper adds only supplementary soldier measurements and does not redescribe their morphology.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head and dorsum of thorax auburn; postclypeus and abdominal tergites argus brown; under surface, legs and antennae clay colour; sternites suffused laterally with Brussels brown; wing membrane a little lighter. Head moderately setose, broadly rounded behind, flat on the summit; eyes large, prominent, coarsely faceted, separated from the lower margin of the head by about one-third of their diameter; ocelli large, broadly oval, close to the eyes; postclypeus moderately convex, half as long as wide, strongly convex behind and truncate in front; labrum narrow at the base, widest in the middle; fontanelle long and narrow, midway between the base of the head and the clypeofrontal suture; antennae 14-jointed, the 3rd joint smallest, the 4th and 5th equal. Pronotum a little narrower than the head, slightly concave and turned up in front, the anterolateral angles broadly rounded, the sides sloping to the rounded posterior margin, the surface densely setose, the marginal setae longest and golden; meso- and metanotum deeply emarginate behind. Wing membrane densely covered with micrasters and bearing numerous setae; radial sector stout, well separated from the radius and setose throughout; wing margin and radial sector very setose except on the proximal third of the hind border. Legs moderately stout and very setose; abdomen nearly parallel-sided, apex pointed, densely clothed with short pale setae; cerci short and stout.
